cases.name: mixed_route_coordinator_capacity_one
proof: Six ordered live-host attempts: Claude coordinator, Codex accepted child, failed Claude child, Claude repair continuation, Codex generation-2 repair, Claude synthesis continuation.
Peak admitted fixture sessions stayed at one. Parent yielded twice, releasing capacity so children could execute.
Repeated child-spawn identity produced three tasks rather than duplicate children. The accepted child executed once.
Captured host tools rejected a child scope outside the parent scope and an out-of-scope file write.
A failed child result reached the coordinator; replacement changed its generation and route, and next-attempt guidance reached the repaired child.
An accepted child artifact was read and imported into the coordinator checkout before another yield. The next continuation retained those imported files.
On continuation 3, a fresh ready wait for the older successful sibling authorizes reading its accepted artifact even though that sibling was absent from the last dispatched wait set.
At a quiescent paused checkpoint, reopening SQLite admitted no work until explicit resume. Completed sibling work was not repeated.

Final artifact contained src/accepted.txt, src/repaired.txt and src/summary.txt. Source files stayed unchanged until accepted-attempt integration; repeated integration preserved the installed result and outside-scope file.
Every retained old managed context rejected late result submission after execution stopped. Observed fixture accounting was zero tokens and zero cost.

cases.name: cancel_unknown_recovery_hold
proof: A live-host attempt wrote only to its private checkout, then deliberately refused to certify stop after cancellation.
The attempt became Unknown, retained its 4096-token admission reservation, blocked the queued successor and refused retry.
Late file and result callbacks were denied. The unaccepted artifact stayed unsealed and source remained untouched.
Reopening SQLite preserved the hold. An unsuccessful reconciliation did not admit the successor.
Only explicit fixture-verified stop plus host reconciliation released the reservation. The successor then ran once through the other route.
There were two fixture turns total and peak active sessions stayed at one.

cases.name: quickjs_live_tool_coordination
proof: QuickJS programmatically created children through journaled host calls, used Claude/Codex-labelled routes and waited for typed results.
The script observed a controlled failed child, added guidance, replaced it with generation 2 on the other route and awaited successful repair.
A declared-dependency synthesis worker imported both accepted artifacts through captured live file tools and submitted its JSON result.
Four fixture turns produced three tasks; the accepted sibling executed once and the repaired child retained both attempt records.
Final script result persisted its input marker and synthesized output. Database reopen preserved Completed state.
Replaying the creation identity and asking to start the completed pinned script produced no additional turns.
Observed fixture accounting was zero tokens and zero cost; peak admitted sessions did not exceed two. Source checkout remained unchanged.

cases.name: runtime_single_owner_lock
proof: A second workflow runtime owner was rejected while the temporary owner lock was held; ownership became available after explicit drop.

additional_regression.name: later_continuation_ready_wait_for_older_successful_sibling
additional_regression.purpose: Verify that a later parent continuation can freshly wait for and access an already-completed sibling artifact, even when that sibling was absent from the last dispatched wait set.

baseline.observed_error: artifact access requires a declared or awaited dependency
baseline.valid_scope: src/accepted.txt is inside the coordinator src scope
baseline.observed_precondition: workflow_wait returned ready for accepted generation 1 on parent continuation 3
baseline.note: The deterministic fixture asserts valid tool calls succeed; its assertion failure left the run Unknown with an admission hold, as required by panic recovery.
